recovery.timeline:
The recovery process after an ankle ligament reconstruction typically takes about 4-6 weeks. Here's what can be expected during this timeline: 
- Week 1-2: You will likely need to keep the affected ankle elevated as much as possible to help reduce swelling and promote healing. During this period, it is important to avoid putting any weight on the affected foot, and you may need crutches for support.
- Week 3-4: Gentle exercises may be introduced under the guidance of a physiotherapist to help restore movement and strength to the ankle. You might transition from crutches to partial weight-bearing under supervision.
- Week 5-6: Gradual weight-bearing and increased activity levels as pain and swelling decrease. By the end of this period, you might begin more intensive physical therapy focused on regaining full leg function and balance.
tips: To minimize swelling and discomfort, apply ice packs to your ankle for 15-20 minutes every couple of hours during the first few days post-surgery.
Keep the leg elevated above heart level whenever possible, especially in the initial days to reduce swelling.
Wear your recovery boot or brace as directed by Dr. Reddy to ensure proper healing of the ligament reconstruction.
Stay consistent with your physiotherapy exercises, as they are crucial for restoring strength and flexibility to your ankle.
recovery.follow_up: You will need regular follow-up appointments with Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy at Apollo Hospitals Hyderabad to monitor your healing process. Generally, these may occur 1-2 weeks post-surgery, then again at 6 weeks, and a final check-up around 12 weeks to ensure proper healing and recovery.

1. **Week 1:** Initially, you'll be asked to rest and keep your knee elevated to reduce swelling. The use of crutches is recommended to avoid putting weight on your knee. You may begin physical therapy with gentle range-of-motion exercises. 
2. **Week 2-3:** Gradually, you can start weight-bearing activities as tolerated and continue with physical therapy to improve flexibility and strength. Driving may be resumed if the right leg was operated on and you feel comfortable. 
3. **Week 4-6:** By this time, most patients can typically return to normal daily activities. Physical therapy will likely intensify to strengthen your knee muscles. By the end of week 6, you should have significant improvement in knee function.
tips: Tip 1: Keep your knee elevated and apply ice packs regularly to manage swelling and pain during the first few days.
Tip 2: Follow your physiotherapist’s exercises diligently to aid in regaining mobility and strength. Each exercise is crucial for a full recovery.
Tip 3: Maintain a balanced diet rich in nutrients to support your body's healing process.
Tip 4: Avoid high-impact activities and twisting motions in the early stages of recovery to prevent re-injury.
recovery.follow_up: You should have a follow-up appointment scheduled with Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy approximately 1-2 weeks after surgery. This visit allows the doctor to assess your healing progress and make any necessary adjustments to your recovery plan. Subsequent visits may be scheduled every few weeks to ensure the knee is healing properly, especially if there are concerns or complications. Apollo Hospitals in Hyderabad provides a well-organized follow-up schedule, and the medical staff will guide you throughout the recovery journey.

faqs.answer: The cost ranges from ₹2.5 to 4.5 lakhs depending on the implant type (standard vs premium), hospital room category, and any additional procedures needed.

faqs.question: Can both knees be replaced at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, bilateral (both knees) replacement can be done in a single surgery for suitable candidates. This reduces overall recovery time and cost.

faqs.question: How long will my knee replacement last?
faqs.answer: Modern knee implants typically last 20-25 years. With proper care and avoiding high-impact activities, many patients never need revision surgery.

faqs.question: When can I drive after knee replacement?
faqs.answer: Most patients can drive an automatic car 4-6 weeks after surgery (left knee) or 6-8 weeks (right knee). You should be off narcotic pain medications.

faqs.question: How long does viscosupplementation last?
faqs.answer: Benefits typically last 6-12 months, though this varies by individual. Some patients have longer-lasting relief, especially with newer single-injection products.

faqs.question: Is viscosupplementation better than cortisone?
faqs.answer: They work differently. Cortisone reduces inflammation quickly but effects fade in weeks. Viscosupplementation lubricates the joint with more gradual but potentially longer-lasting benefits.

faqs.question: Can I have viscosupplementation in my hip?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it's used less commonly in the hip than the knee. The hip injection requires ultrasound or X-ray guidance for accuracy.
